question: What protective effect is claimed for the body of one who has practiced, even in the case of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison would normally enter the body in such a case.
By force of this practice, poison does not enter the body.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
uncertainties: Scope and limits of this protection not specified
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
